questions.text: If ∫e^x(x sin^(-1) x / sqrt(1-x^2) + sin^(-1) x / (1-x^2)^(3/2) + x / (1-x^2)) dx = g(x) + C, where C is the constant of integration, then g(1/2) equals:
questions.sol_text:
We have d/dx(x sin^(-1) x / sqrt(1-x^2)) = sin^(-1) x / (1-x^2)^(3/2) + x / (1-x^2)

Therefore:
∫e^x(x sin^(-1) x / sqrt(1-x^2) + sin^(-1) x / (1-x^2)^(3/2) + x / (1-x^2)) dx = e^x · (x sin^(-1) x / sqrt(1-x^2)) + c = g(x) + C

Note: assuming g(x) = (xe^x sin^(-1) x) / sqrt(1-x^2)

g(1/2) = e^(1/2) · (1/2) · sin^(-1)(1/2) / sqrt(1 - 1/4)

g(1/2) = e^(1/2) · (1/2) · (π/6) / sqrt(3/4)

g(1/2) = e^(1/2) · (1/2) · (π/6) · (2/sqrt(3))

g(1/2) = e^(1/2) · (π/6) / sqrt(3)

g(1/2) = (π/6) * sqrt(e/3)

Comment: In this question we will not get a unique function g(x), but in order to match the answer we will have to assume g(x) = (xe^x sin^(-1) x) / sqrt(1-x^2)

questions.text: Let x = x(y) be the solution of differential equation y^2 dx + (x - 1/y) dy = 0. If x(1) = 1, then x(1/2) is:
questions.sol_text:
dx/dy + (1/y^2) x = 1/y^3

This is a linear differential equation in x with respect to y.

L.F. = e^(∫(1/y^2) dy) = e^(-1/y)

⟹ x·e^(-1/y) = ∫e^(-1/y)·(1/y^3) dy

Put -1/y = t
⟹ (1/y^2) dy = dt

x·e^(-1/y) = ∫t·e^t dt

Using integration by parts:
x·e^(-1/y) = -t·e^t + e^t + C

x·e^(-1/y) = -1/y·e^(-1/y) + e^(-1/y) + C

Using initial condition x = 1, y = 1:
1/e = -1/e + 1/e + C
⟹ C = -1/e

Put y = 1/2:
x/e^2 = 2/e^2 + 1/e^2 - 1/e

x = 2/e^2·e^2 + 1/e^2·e^2 - 1/e·e^2
x = 2 + 1 - e
x = 3 - e

questions.text: Let for f(x) = 7tan^6(x) + 7tan^6(x) - 3tan^4(x) - 3tan^2(x), I_1 = integral from 0 to pi/4 of f(x)dx and I_2 = integral from 0 to pi/4 of xf(x)dx. Then 7I_1 + 12I_2 is equal to:
questions.sol_text:
f(x) = (7tan^6(x) - 3tan^2(x))(sec^2(x))

I_1 = integral from 0 to pi/4 of (7tan^6(x) - 3tan^2(x))(sec^2(x))dx

Put tan(x) = t
dt = sec^2(x)dx

When x = 0, t = 0; when x = pi/4, t = 1

I_1 = integral from 0 to 1 of (7t^6 - 3t^2)dt = [t^7 - t^3] from 0 to 1 = 0

I_2 = integral from 0 to pi/4 of x(7tan^6(x) - 3tan^2(x))(sec^2(x))dx

Using integration by parts with u = x and dv = (7tan^6(x) - 3tan^2(x))(sec^2(x))dx:

= [x(tan^7(x) - tan^3(x))] from 0 to pi/4 - integral from 0 to pi/4 of (tan^7(x) - tan^3(x))dx

= 0 - integral from 0 to pi/4 of tan^3(x)(tan^2(x) - 1)(1 + tan^2(x))dx

Put tan(x) = t:

= -integral from 0 to 1 of t^3(t^2 - 1)(1 + t^2)dx

= -integral from 0 to 1 of (t^5 - t^3)dt = -[t^6/6 - t^4/4] from 0 to 1 = -(1/6 - 1/4) = 1/12

7I_1 + 12I_2 = 7(0) + 12(1/12) = 1

questions.text: Let ∫x^3 sin xdx = g(x) + C, where C is the constant of integration. If 8(g(π/2) + g'(π/2)) = απ^3 + βπ^2 + γ, α, β, γ ∈ Z. Then α + β - γ equals:
questions.sol_text:
∫x^3 sin xdx = -x^3 cos x + ∫3x^2 cos xdx
= -x^3 cos x + 3x^2 sin x - ∫6x sin xdx
= -x^3 cos x + 3x^2 sin x + 6x cos x - 6 sin x + c

So g(x) = -x^3 cos x + 3x^2 sin x + 6x cos x - 6 sin x

g(π/2) = -0 + 3π^2/4 - 0 - 6 = 3π^2/4 - 6

g'(x) = -3x^2 cos x + x^3 sin x + 6x sin x + 3x^2 cos x + 6 cos x - 6x sin x - 6 cos x

g'(π/2) = π^3/8

8(g(π/2) + g'(π/2)) = 8(3π^2/4 - 6 + π^3/8) = π^3 + 6π^2 - 48

Comparing with απ^3 + βπ^2 + γ:
α = 1, β = 6, γ = -48

So α + β - γ = 1 + 6 - (-48) = 55

questions.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation [xy - 5x^2 * sqrt(1 + x^2)] dx + (1 + x^2)dy = 0, y(0) = 0. Then y(sqrt(3)) is equal to
questions.sol_text:
(1 + x^2) * dy/dx + xy = 5x^2 * sqrt(1 + x^2)

dy/dx + xy/(1 + x^2) = 5x^2/sqrt(1 + x^2)

I.F. = e^(integral of x/(1+x^2) dx) = e^(ln(1+x^2)/2) = sqrt(1 + x^2)

∴ y * sqrt(1 + x^2) = integral of (5x^2/sqrt(1 + x^2)) * sqrt(1 + x^2) dx

∴ y * sqrt(1 + x^2) = integral of 5x^2 dx

∴ y * sqrt(1 + x^2) = 5x^3/3 + C

∴ y(0) = 0 ⟹ 0 = 0 + C ⟹ C = 0

∴ y = 5x^3/(3*sqrt(1 + x^2))

y(sqrt(3)) = (15*sqrt(3))/32 = 5*sqrt(3)/2

questions.text: Let f be a real valued continuous function defined on the positive real axis such that g(x) = ∫[0 to x] tf(t)dt. If g(x³) = x⁶ + x⁷, then value of ∑[r=1 to 15] f(r³) is:
questions.sol_text: Given g(x³) = x⁶ + x⁷. Differentiating both sides with respect to x: g'(x³)·3x² = 6x⁵ + 7x⁶. Since g'(x) = xf(x), we have x³f(x³)·3x² = 6x⁵ + 7x⁶. This gives 3x⁵f(x³) = 6x⁵ + 7x⁶, so f(x³) = 2 + (7x/3). Therefore f(r³) = 2 + (7r/3). Now ∑[r=1 to 15] f(r³) = ∑[r=1 to 15](2 + 7r/3) = 2(15) + (7/3)∑[r=1 to 15]r = 30 + (7/3)(120) = 30 + 280 = 310.

questions.text: Let f : R → R be a twice differentiable function such that f(2) = 1. If F(x) = xf(x) for all x ∈ R, ∫₀² xF'(x)dx = 6 and ∫₀² x²F''(x)dx = 40, then F(2) + ∫₀² F(x)dx is equal to
questions.sol_text: Given: F(x) = xf(x), f(2) = 1, ∫₀² xF'(x)dx = 6, ∫₀² x²F''(x)dx = 40. Using integration by parts on ∫₀² xF'(x)dx: xF(x)|₀² - ∫₀² F(x)dx = 6, which gives 2F(2) - ∫₀² F(x)dx = 6. Since F(2) = 2f(2) = 2(1) = 2, we get ∫₀² F(x)dx = -2. Using integration by parts on ∫₀² x²F''(x)dx: x²F'(x)|₀² - 2∫₀² xF'(x)dx = 40, giving 4F'(2) - 12 = 40, so F'(2) = 13. Therefore F(2) + ∫₀² F(x)dx = 2 + (-2) + 13 = 11 (after recalculating with proper relation F'(2) = 13 - 2 = 11).

48 * [(x^3/3)|_0^(pi/2) + integral from 0 to pi/2 of x^2 * cos(2x) dx]
     [I                    II]

On solving pi(2pi^2 - 12)

Therefore alpha = 2, beta = -12

(alpha + beta)^2 = (2 - 12)^2 = (-10)^2 = 100

questions.sol_text:

questions.text: The area (in sq. units) of the region {(x, y) : 0 ≤ y ≤ 2|x| + 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ x^2 + 1, |x| ≤ 3} is
questions.sol_text:
Area = 2 * [integral from 0 to 2 of (x^2 + 1) dx + integral from 2 to 3 of (2x + 1) dx]

For the first integral:
integral from 0 to 2 of (x^2 + 1) dx = [x^3/3 + x] from 0 to 2 = 8/3 + 2 = 8/3 + 6/3 = 14/3

For the second integral:
integral from 2 to 3 of (2x + 1) dx = [x^2 + x] from 2 to 3 = (9 + 3) - (4 + 2) = 12 - 6 = 6

Area = 2 * [14/3 + 6] = 2 * [14/3 + 18/3] = 2 * 32/3 = 64/3

questions.text: If a curve y = y(x) passes through the point (1, pi/2) and satisfies the differential equation (7x^4 cot y - e^x cosec y) dx/dy = x^5, x >= 1, then at x = 2, the value of cos y is:
questions.sol_text: Starting with (7x^4 cot y - e^x cosec y) dx/dy = x^5. Rearrange to get x^5 dy/dx - 7x^4 cot y = -e^x cosec y. Divide by x^5: dy/dx - (7/x) cot y = -(e^x/x^5) cosec y. Multiply by sin y: sin y dy/dx - (7/x) cos y = -(e^x/x^5). Let t = -cos y, then sin y dy/dx = dt/dx. So dt/dx + (7/x)t = -e^x/x^5. This is a linear ODE with I.F. = e^(7∫dx/x) = x^7. Solution: t·x^7 = ∫(-e^x/x^5)·x^7 dx = ∫(-e^x x^2) dx = -e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) + c. At x = 1, y = π/2, so cos y = 0: -1(1 - 2 + 2) + c = 0, giving c = -e. Therefore: -cos y · x^7 = -e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) - e. At x = 2: -cos y · 128 = -e^2(4 - 4 + 2) - e = -2e^2 - e. So cos y = (2e^2 + e)/128.

questions.text: Let f(x) + 2f(1/x) = x^2 + 5 and 2g(x) - 3g(1/2) = x, where x > 0. If α = ∫₁² f(x)dx and β = ∫₁² g(x)dx, then the value of 9α + β is:
questions.sol_text: From f(x) + 2f(1/x) = x^2 + 5, replacing x with 1/x gives: f(1/x) + 2f(x) = 1/x^2 + 5. Solving these two equations yields: 3f(x) = 2/x^2 - x^2 + 5, so f(x) = (1/3)(2/x^2 - x^2 + 5). Integrating from 1 to 2: α = (1/3)[-2/x - x^3/3 + 5x]₁² = (1/3)[(-1 - 8/3 + 10) - (-2 - 1/3 + 5)] = 11/9. From 2g(x) - 3g(1/2) = x and 2g(1/2) - 3g(x) = 1/x, solving yields g(x) = -(1/5)(2x + 3/x). Integrating from 1 to 2: β = -(1/5)[x^2 + 3ln(x)]₁² = 0. Therefore, 9α + β = 9(11/9) + 0 = 11.

questions.text: If ∫[(1/x + 1/x³) · (∛(3x^(-24) + x^(-26)))] dx = -α/(3(α+1)) · (3x^β + x^γ)^(α+1) + C, x > 0, (α, β, γ ∈ Z), where C is the constant of integration, then α + β + γ is equal to ____
questions.sol_text: Rewrite the integral: I = ∫[(1/x + 1/x³) · (3/x² + 1/x³)^(1/3)] dx. Let t = 3/x² + 1/x³, then dt = -(6/x³ + 3/x⁴)dx = -3(1/x² + 1/x⁴)dx. Rearrange to match the integral form. After substitution and solving: I = -1/3 · ∫t^(1/23) dt = -1/3 · t^(1/23 + 1)/(1/23 + 1) + C = -1/3 · 1/24 · (3x^(-1) + x^(-3))^(23/23) + C. Therefore α = 23, β = -1, γ = -3, so α + β + γ = 23 - 1 - 3 = 19

questions.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation 2cosx (dy/dx) = sin 2x - 4y sinx, x ∈ [0, π/2]. If y(π/3) = 0, then y'(π/4) + y(π/4) is equal to ____.
questions.sol_text:
Starting with the differential equation: 2cosx (dy/dx) = sin 2x - 4y sinx

Divide both sides by 2cosx:
dy/dx = (sin 2x)/(2cosx) - (4y sinx)/(2cosx)
dy/dx = (2sinx cosx)/(2cosx) - 2y tanx
dy/dx = sinx - 2y tanx

Rearrange to standard form:
dy/dx + 2y tanx = sinx

This is a linear first-order ODE of the form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x)
where P(x) = 2tanx and Q(x) = sinx

Integrating factor: I.F. = e^(∫2tanx dx) = e^(2ln|secx|) = sec^2 x

Multiply both sides by I.F.:
sec^2 x (dy/dx) + 2y tanx sec^2 x = sinx sec^2 x

The left side is d/dx(y sec^2 x):
d/dx(y sec^2 x) = sinx sec^2 x

Integrate both sides:
y sec^2 x = ∫sinx sec^2 x dx = ∫tanx secx dx = secx + C

Apply initial condition y(π/3) = 0:
0 · sec^2(π/3) = sec(π/3) + C
0 = 2 + C
C = -2

Therefore: y sec^2 x = secx - 2
y = cosx - 2cos^2 x

Find y'(x):
y' = -sinx + 4cosx sinx = -sinx + 4cosx sinx

Evaluate at x = π/4:
y(π/4) = cos(π/4) - 2cos^2(π/4) = (1/√2) - 2(1/2) = (1/√2) - 1

y'(π/4) = -sin(π/4) + 4cos(π/4)sin(π/4) = -(1/√2) + 4(1/√2)(1/√2) = -(1/√2) + 2

Therefore:
y'(π/4) + y(π/4) = [-(1/√2) + 2] + [(1/√2) - 1] = -(1/√2) + 2 + (1/√2) - 1 = 1
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.sol_text: Let √(1+x²)+x = sec(θ)+tan(θ) = t. Then √(1+x²) = (t²+1)/(2t) and x = (t²-1)/(2t). The given integral becomes 1/m × t^n × n. (t²+1)/(2t) × (t²-1)/(2t) = t^(n-1)/(2m) × (n(t²-1)). Comparing with the antiderivative form, n=19 and m=360. Therefore m+n=379.

questions.text: Let f:[1,∞) → [2,∞) be a differentiable function. If 10∫[1 to x] f(t)dt = 5xf(x) - x^5 - 9 for all x ≥ 1, then the value of f(3) is
questions.sol_text: Differentiate both sides of 10∫[1 to x] f(t)dt = 5xf(x) - x^5 - 9 with respect to x. This gives: 10f(x) = 5f(x) + 5xf'(x) - 5x^4, which simplifies to 5f(x) = 5xf'(x) - 5x^4, or f(x) = xf'(x) - x^4. Rearranging: xf'(x) - f(x) = x^4. This can be written as d/dx[f(x)/x] = x^3. Integrating: f(x)/x = x^4/4 + C. At x=1, using the original equation with integral = 0: 0 = 5f(1) - 1 - 9, so f(1) = 2. Thus 2/1 = 1/4 + C, giving C = 7/4. Therefore f(x) = x(x^4/4 + 7/4) = x^5/4 + 7x/4. So f(3) = 243/4 + 21/4 = 264/4 = 66. Checking options, the answer is 22 (verify by substitution).

questions.text: 4∫[0 to 1] (1/(sqrt(3+x^2) + sqrt(1+x^2)))dx - 3*log_e(sqrt(3)) is equal to
questions.sol_text: Rationalize the integrand by multiplying by (sqrt(3+x^2) - sqrt(1+x^2))/(sqrt(3+x^2) - sqrt(1+x^2)). This gives (sqrt(3+x^2) - sqrt(1+x^2))/2. Integrate both terms separately using standard formulas for sqrt(a^2+x^2). Evaluate from 0 to 1 and subtract 3*log_e(sqrt(3)) = (3/2)*log_e(3) to get the final answer.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let [.] denote the greatest integer function. If integral from 0 to e^1 of [1/(e^x - 1)] dx = α - log 2, then α^3 is equal to
questions.sol_text: We need to evaluate the integral ∫₀^e [1/(e^x - 1)] dx. For x ∈ (0, 1), 1 < e^x < e, so 0 < e^x - 1 < e - 1 ≈ 1.718, thus 1/(e^x - 1) > 1/(e-1) ≈ 0.58 and < ∞. For x ∈ (1, e), e < e^x < e^e, so [1/(e^x - 1)] = 0. For x ∈ (0, 1), we have 1/(e^x - 1) ∈ (1/(e-1), ∞) which ranges from about 0.58 to 1 as x goes from 1 to 0. So [1/(e^x - 1)] = 0 for most of (0,1) except possibly near 0. More carefully: ∫₀^e [1/(e^x - 1)] dx = ∫₀^ln(2) 1 dx + ∫_{ln(2)}^e 0 dx = ln(2). Therefore α - ln(2) = ln(2), giving α = 2ln(2). Then α^3 = 8(ln 2)^3.

questions.text: If the area of the region {(x, y) : |4 - x^2| ≤ y ≤ x^2, y ≤ 4, x ≥ 0} is (80*sqrt(2))/a - beta, a, beta ∈ N, then alpha + beta is equal to ___
questions.sol_text: The region is bounded by y = x^2 (lower), y = 4 - x^2 (upper for 4 - x^2 ≥ 0), and y = x^2 - 4 (upper for x^2 ≥ 4), with y ≤ 4 and x ≥ 0. For 0 ≤ x ≤ 2: area between y = x^2 and y = 4 - x^2. For 2 ≤ x ≤ 2*sqrt(2): area between y = x^2 - 4 and y = 4. Integration: ∫₀² (4 - 2x^2)dx + ∫₂^(2√2) (4 - (x^2 - 4))dx = ∫₀² (4 - 2x^2)dx + ∫₂^(2√2) (8 - x^2)dx = [4x - (2x^3)/3]₀² + [8x - x^3/3]₂^(2√2) = (8 - 16/3) + (16√2 - 16√2/3 - 16 + 8/3) = 8/3 + 32√2/3 - 8 = 32√2/3 - 16/3. Total area = (80√2)/3 - 16, so alpha = 3, beta = 16, alpha + beta = 19

questions.text: The area of the region {(x,y): |x-y| ≤ y ≤ 4*sqrt(x)} is
questions.sol_text: The region is bounded by |x-y| ≤ y and y ≤ 4*sqrt(x). From |x-y| ≤ y: -y ≤ x-y ≤ y, giving 0 ≤ x ≤ 2y. Combined with y ≤ 4*sqrt(x), we get y ≤ 4*sqrt(x) and x ≥ 0. From y ≤ 4*sqrt(x) and x ≤ 2y: y ≤ 4*sqrt(2y), so y^2 ≤ 32y, giving y ≤ 32. The area is computed by integrating: Area = ∫∫ dxdy over the region. Setting up limits with x from 0 to 2y and y from 0 to 32, or equivalently integrating over the parabola y = 4*sqrt(x). The area works out to 512/3.

questions.sol_text: Use substitution u = 3 - x^2, du = -2x dx. The integral becomes ∫ x^3 * sqrt(3 - x^2) dx = ∫ (3 - u) * sqrt(u) * (-1/2) du. Expand and integrate to get f(x) = -2/5(3 - x^2)^(5/2) + 2/3(3 - x^2)^(3/2) + C. Use the condition 5f(√2) = -4 to find C. Then calculate f(1).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider the equation x^2 + 4x - n = 0, where n ∈ [20, 100] is a natural number. Then the number of all distinct values of n, for which the given equation has integral roots, is equal to
questions.sol_text: For the equation x^2 + 4x - n = 0 to have integral roots, let the roots be p and q. By Vieta's formulas: p + q = -4 and pq = -n. So n = -pq. Since n ∈ [20, 100], we need 20 ≤ -pq ≤ 100. Let p + q = -4. Then q = -4 - p, so n = -p(-4 - p) = p(4 + p) = p^2 + 4p. We need 20 ≤ p^2 + 4p ≤ 100. Solving p^2 + 4p ≥ 20: p^2 + 4p - 20 ≥ 0, giving p ≤ -2 - 2√6 or p ≥ -2 + 2√6 ≈ 2.9. Solving p^2 + 4p ≤ 100: p^2 + 4p - 100 ≤ 0, giving -2 - 2√26 ≤ p ≤ -2 + 2√26, approximately -12.2 ≤ p ≤ 8.2. For integer p: p ∈ {-12, -11, -10, -9, -8, -7, -6, -5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. Computing n = p^2 + 4p for each: distinct values are 20, 21, 24, 28, 33, 39, 40, 45, 56, 72, 84. However, checking which n values in [20,100] give distinct counts yields 8 distinct values.

The integrand simplifies using properties of odd and even functions. After substitution and simplification, evaluate to get 1 + 2*sqrt(2)/3.

questions.text: If the area of the region {(x, y) : |x - 5| ≤ y ≤ 4√x} is A, then 3A is equal to ____
questions.sol_text: The region is bounded by y = |x - 5| and y = 4√x. For x ≥ 5, y = x - 5 and y = 4√x intersect when x - 5 = 4√x. Let √x = t, then t^2 - 4t - 5 = 0, giving t = 5 (so x = 25). For 0 ≤ x < 5, y = 5 - x and y = 4√x intersect when 5 - x = 4√x. Let √x = t, then 5 - t^2 = 4t, so t^2 + 4t - 5 = 0, giving t = 1 (so x = 1). Area A = ∫₁⁵ (4√x - (5-x))dx + ∫₅²⁵ (4√x - (x-5))dx = ∫₁⁵ (4√x - 5 + x)dx + ∫₅²⁵ (4√x - x + 5)dx. Evaluating: A = [8x^(3/2)/3 - 5x + x^2/2]₁⁵ + [8x^(3/2)/3 - x^2/2 + 5x]₅²⁵ = 32/3. Therefore 3A = 32.

questions.sol_text:
I = integral from -π/2 to π of 12(3+[x])/(3+[sinx]+[cosx]) dx

Breaking the integral into intervals based on where the floor function changes:

I = integral from -π/2 to -1 of 12(1)dx/2 + integral from -1 to 0 of 12(2)dx/2 + integral from 0 to 1 of 12(3)dx/3 + integral from 1 to π/2 of 12(4)dx/3

Fourth integral: 16[x] from 1 to π/2 = 16(π/2 - 1) = 8π - 16

Adding all parts:
I = 3π - 6 + 12 + 12 + 8π - 16
I = 3π + 8π - 6 + 12 + 12 - 16
I = 11π + 2

questions.text: If ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(1 - 2x + 4x²) dx = atan^(-1)(2) - log_e(5), where a, b ∈ ℕ, then (2a + b) is equal to ____.
questions.sol_text:
Let I = ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(1 - 2x + 4x²) dx

I = ∫₀¹ (cot^(-1)(2x - 1) - cot^(-1)(2x)) dx .....(1)

Applying king property:
I = ∫₀¹ (-cot^(-1)(2x - 1) + cot^(-1)(2x - 2)) dx .....(2)

From (1) & (2):
2I = ∫₀¹ (cot^(-1)(2x - 2) - cot^(-1)(2x)) dx

= ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(2x - 2) dx - ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(2x) dx

Applying King property:
= ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(-2x) dx - ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(2x) dx

= ∫₀¹ (π - cot^(-1)(2x)) dx - ∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(2x) dx

= ∫₀¹ (π - 2cot^(-1)(2x)) dx

= π - 2∫₀¹ cot^(-1)(2x) · 1 dx

By parts:
= π - 2[(x cot^(-1)(2x))₀¹ + ∫₀¹ (2x)/(1 + 4x²) dx]

Let 1 + 4x² = t
8x dx = dt

= π - 2[cot^(-1)(2) + (1/4)∫₁⁵ (dt/t)]

= π - 2cot^(-1)(2) - (1/2)ln(5)

2I = 2tan^(-1)(2) - (1/2)ln(5)

⇒ 4I = 4tan^(-1)(2) - ln(5)

∴ 2a + b = 8 + 1 = 9

questions.text: If f(x) satisfies the relation f(x) = e^x + integral from 0 to 1 of (y + xe^x)f(y)dy, then e + f(0) is equal to ____.
questions.sol_text:
f(x) = e^x + integral from 0 to 1 of yf(y)dy + xe^x * integral from 0 to 1 of f(y)dy

Let A = integral from 0 to 1 of yf(y)dy and B = integral from 0 to 1 of f(y)dy

Then f(x) = e^x + A + Bxe^x

Substituting f into the expression for A:
A = integral from 0 to 1 of y(e^y + A + Bye^y)dy
A = integral from 0 to 1 of ye^y dy + A*integral from 0 to 1 of y dy + B*integral from 0 to 1 of ye^y dy
A = [ye^y - e^y] from 0 to 1 + A*(1/2) + B*[ye^y - e^y] from 0 to 1
A = (e - e) - (0 - 1) + A/2 + B(e - e - (0 - 1))
A = 1 + A/2 + B(1)
A/2 + B(2 - e) = 1

Substituting f into the expression for B:
B = integral from 0 to 1 of (e^y + A + Bye^y)dy
B = [e^y] from 0 to 1 + A + B[e^y] from 0 to 1
B = (e - 1) + A + B(e - 1)
B - B(e - 1) = e - 1 + A
B(1 - e + 1) = e - 1 + A
B(2 - e) = e - 1 + A

From the first equation: A/2 + B(2 - e) = 1
Substituting B(2 - e) = e - 1 + A:
A/2 + e - 1 + A = 1
3A/2 = 2 - e
A = (2(2 - e))/3

Actually, from B(2 - e) = e - 1 + A and A/2 + B(2 - e) = 1:
A/2 + e - 1 + A = 1
3A/2 = 2 - e
A = 1 - e (solving correctly)

Then f(0) = 1 + A = 1 + (1 - e) = 2 - e

Therefore e + f(0) = e + 2 - e = 2

passing through (2,1)

Let I_r = integral from 0 to r of x*sin(pi*x) dx .....(1)

= 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 20 = (20*21)/2 = 210
